![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The "Retry" action's `onClick` handler calls `handleOpenFolder` recursively. Since `handleOpenFolder` does not have its own loading state, if the underlying `api.app.openInExplorer` call fails consistently, a user clicking "Retry" will immediately trigger another failure and another toast. This can be spammed, leading to a poor user experience. Consider adding a loading state to `handleOpenFolder` to prevent re-entrancy or debouncing the retry action.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The "Retry" action for `saveSettings` calls the function recursively from within its own `catch` block. This pattern is also present for `saveRepositoryRoots` and `startMcp`. This can lead to confusing behavior and allows the user to spam the action if it fails repeatedly. While the `isSaving` state prevents some re-entrancy for the main button, the toast action is independent. A better approach would be to manage the retry action's state separately or debounce it to provide a more robust user experience. Additionally, using the `void` operator here is unconventional; `() => saveSettings()` is more standard.
